items.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001
items.q: the first people like I think I mentioned before that I heard, it was like you know Bird and Bud and Miles and Tommy Flanagan...

ctx.x: Have you had occasion where you’ve tried experimenting with maybe some substitutions and so forth with different singers, and you find that — not to do it.

Well I don’t really play with singers but you know the first thing that I always tell, and not everyone does this so you don’t have to do this, you know the way Herbie was playing behind Miles. Sometimes it sounds, he’s just got his rhythmic thing, and it’s so much fun, seemingly having nothing to do with Miles you know. So you could play that way too. He was hooking up a lot with the rhythm section and I’m sure that’s what Miles wanted at that time, if we’re thinking back into the mid-60s. But I always, when I’m…
You’ve had pretty good success it seems with your recording career. Is it a challenge? Is it difficult to get records out and has it changed over the years?
